predictions.question: C₄ᵥ 的二维极向量沿x，母群轨道包含几个不同方向？
predictions.explanation: 母群阶数8，保持该非零向量的稳定子群阶数2，轨道数为8/2=4。不是每个操作都产生新方向。

predictions.question: 给立方极向量加入 −h_xη_x 后，六个母群轴向轨道态还全部等能吗？
choices: 否，外场降低能量函数的对称性
predictions.explanation: 该预设h_x=0.3，使+x、−x与垂直x的四个方向出现三种能量。母群轨道不等于外场后全部简并畴。

lessons.title: From order-parameter directions to surviving operations and domains
lessons.summary: Calculate separately the symmetry of a specified state, the symmetry of its energy function, and its orbit of equivalent states.

sections.title: Specify the representation first
sections.text: In this experiment the order parameter is a two-dimensional polar vector of C₄ᵥ or a three-dimensional polar vector of O_h. Point-group matrices act on η; inversion of an O_h polar vector is −I. Oxygen-octahedron rotations are axial vectors, so this inversion rule cannot be applied directly.

sections.title: State  stabilizer subgroup
sections.text: Test D(g)η=η operation by operation; the surviving operations form the stabilizer subgroup. The zero vector preserves the parent group, while a nonzero direction can lower symmetry. Comparisons use a numerical tolerance of 1e−9, with the actual matrices generated as exact integers.

sections.title: An orbit is not an operation list
sections.text: Different operations may send η to the same direction, so duplicates must be removed. O_h generates six directions along coordinate axes and eight along body diagonals, arising from different  stabilizer subgroup . Specifying a direction alone does not prove a free-energy minimum there.

sections.title: Material connections and limitations
sections.text: Axial or diagonal BaTiO₃ polarization directions provide visual context. This tool does not automatically construct actual atomic displacements, space-group subgroups, translational domains, or experimental phase diagrams. Use the structural-distortion and phase-transition modules to study specified modes and energies.

lessons.title: Derive allowed free-energy terms using each  generator
lessons.summary: Generate independent invariants by monomial group averaging, then use actual coefficients to plot energy-surface sections.

sections.title: Start with one monomial
sections.text: Apply all group operations to monomials such as η_x² and average. Monomials canceled by signs produce no invariant; equivalent monomials give repeated orbit sums. Retain independent orbit sums, optionally normalized to minimal integer coefficients.

sections.title: Constraints have traceable origins
sections.text: Click a coefficient relation to inspect the generator matrix and the exponents and signs before and after transformation. A mirror reverses the sign of η_xη_y, forcing its coefficient to zero; a fourfold rotation requires equal coefficients for η_x² and η_y².

sections.title: Allowed forms do not determine coefficients
sections.text: C₄ᵥ has 1,2,2 independent invariants at orders two, four and six; O_h has 1,2,3. Coefficients are teaching inputs whose signs and magnitudes are not determined by symmetry. Continuous isotropy at second order can be an accidental feature of a low-order truncation.
sections.formula: F = a₂ I₂ + b₄ I₄a + c₄ I₄b + d₆ I₆a + e₆ I₆b + f₆ I₆c

sections.title: Radial minima and full stability
sections.text: Solve for every real stationary point of the one-variable polynomial along the selected direction. These are not all minima of the multidimensional free energy. The angular scan fixes the xy radius and z component; a flat curve or local minimum alone cannot establish a thermodynamic phase. Highest-order boundedness is checked using sufficient conditions, with limitations stated when they fail.

lessons.title: Explicit symmetry breaking, domain energies and coordinate conventions
lessons.summary: Distinguish physically changing an external field from passively changing coordinate notation.

sections.title: An external field does not automatically preserve the parent group
sections.text: With a fixed linear field along laboratory x, retain only operations that also preserve the field. The parent-group orbit remains useful for comparison, but its different directions may split in energy.

sections.title: Distinguishing three groups
sections.text: Inspect separately parent group G, the field-preserving energy-symmetry group G_h, and the intersection preserving both field and state. A state's  stabilizer subgroup  alone does not establish spontaneous symmetry breaking of the entire Hamiltonian.

sections.title: Passive coordinate transformation
sections.text: The columns of Q are new coordinate axes expressed in old coordinates. η, the field, group matrices and energy expression must all transform together. Rotating only the order parameter while leaving the energy anisotropy unchanged generally changes the physical state.
sections.formula: η′ = Qᵀη；D′ = Qᵀ D Q；F′(η′) = F(Qη′)

sections.title: Verify rather than compare entries one by one
sections.text: Compare energy,  stabilizer subgroup  order, and the  covariance residual  of operation actions in both coordinate systems. Matrix entries may change; energy and orbit counts are the quantities to preserve here.

exercises.title: Infer the stabilizer from six axial directions
exercises.prompt: Use the cubic-axis preset: derive first, then calculate.

steps.prompt: What is the  polar vector  inversion matrix of O_h?
steps.hint: A polar vector changes sign under inversion.
steps.explanation: Inversion maps a nonzero  polarity  vector η to −η.

steps.prompt: How many distinct axial directions can be generated from (0,0,1)?
steps.hint: Count both signs along each of three coordinate axes.

steps.prompt: The parent group has order 48 and the orbit has size 6. What is the stabilizer's order?
steps.explanation: 48/6=8; the current direction's  point group  is C₄ᵥ.

steps.prompt: Does specifying η along z already prove an equilibrium ferroelectric phase?
steps.hint: State symmetry and energy minimization are different checks.
choices: No; energy and full stability analysis are still required
It proves stability at every temperature
It is enough to see that η is nonzero
steps.explanation: Check energy, curvature, and model validity; orbit counting alone does not determine a phase diagram.

exercises.title: Use mirrors and rotations to rule out incorrect free energies
exercises.prompt: Build the allowed terms step by step for a C₄ᵥ two-dimensional polar vector.

steps.prompt: How does η_xη_y transform under the xz mirror?
steps.hint: η_x is unchanged and η_y changes sign.
steps.explanation: Thus, if this term occurs alone, its coefficient must vanish.

steps.prompt: What constraint does a fourfold rotation place on aη_x²+bη_y²?
steps.hint: The energy must be unchanged when the two terms are exchanged.
choices: Both a and b must vanish
steps.explanation: Rotation requires equal coefficients for the two quadratic terms.

steps.prompt: Which pair gives two independent fourth-order invariants?
steps.hint: Check the mirror and fourfold rotation.
choices: η_x⁴ and η_y⁴ are independently invariant
steps.explanation: Orbit sums provide two linearly independent fourth-order invariants.

steps.prompt: What does symmetry allowance of c₄ mean?
choices: Its value still requires a physical model or input
steps.explanation: Symmetry constraints determine the form, not numerical parameter values for a real material.

exercises.title: Distinguish field-driven changes from coordinate changes
exercises.prompt: Use the external-field preset and the general-direction coordinate-change preset.

steps.prompt: After adding −h_xη_x with h_x>0, which of ±x has lower energy?
steps.hint: Parent-group invariants agree for +x and −x, while the linear term differs.
steps.explanation: +x has negative linear field energy and lies below −x.

steps.prompt: With an external field, can all six parent-group axial states still be called degenerate domains?
choices: No; the external field can split the parent-group orbit
Yes, because there are still 6 spatial directions
steps.explanation: Use the symmetry group of the energy function with the field included to determine symmetry-protected energy equivalence.

steps.prompt: How should the group matrices transform in the new coordinates defined by Q?
steps.explanation: The order parameter and operations must change basis consistently to preserve their action.

steps.prompt: What should remain invariant under a passive coordinate change?
steps.hint: The matrix entries need not be identical.
steps.explanation: Invariant results are preserved; coordinate components and matrix entries generally change.

cases.title: Cubic  polarity   order parameter  and ferroelectric domain directions
cases.summary: Compare residual point groups and orbit sizes for a cubic polar vector along an axis, face diagonal, and body diagonal, then connect them to a specified structural distortion.
cases.assumption: Only the polarization-direction  point group  picture is used. No BaTiO₃ parameters are fitted, and no material-specific temperature sequence, atomic modes, or complete  space group  are derived.

cases.title: In-plane ordering directions in a fourfold environment
cases.summary: At a fixed order-parameter length, compare axial and diagonal energies and examine fourth- and sixth-order anisotropy.
cases.assumption: An abstract C₄ᵥ two-dimensional polar vector does not automatically describe arbitrary surface magnetic order; axial magnetic order requires a newly specified representation.

cases.title: Field selection and one experiment in two coordinate systems
cases.kind: Explicit symmetry breaking and convention comparisons
cases.summary: Select a direction with an external field, then rotate the vector, field, operations, and energy consistently to distinguish physical changes from coordinate changes.
cases.assumption: Uniform  order parameter  and an illustrative linear field, without  domain wall  motion, hysteresis dynamics, physical electric-field units, or inversion of measured data.
